edges.description: The model reproduces the visual deficit, the retinal ganglion cell loss behind optic atrophy, and the axonal transport defect proposed to cause it.
edges.limitations: The auditory neuropathy that gives this disease its name is not among the reported mouse phenotypes, so the model speaks to the optic arm and not the auditory one; and the allele is a single missense substitution, not the compound genotypes most patients carry.

edges.description: Mitochondrial iron overload with membrane depolarization was shown in this model, where the founding human evidence for it was indirect.
edges.limitations: Measured in mouse tissue rather than in patient tissue, so the quantitative extent in human disease remains unknown.

nodes.description: Preclinical only. Systemic delivery of a neurotropic AAV-PHP.B vector carrying the mouse Fdxr cDNA to the R389Q mouse prevented optic atrophy, improved sciatic nerve conduction and mobility, and restored mitochondrial complex function. No human trial exists.

evidence.reference_title: Systemic Delivery of AAV-Fdxr Mitigates the Phenotypes of Mitochondrial Disorders in Fdxr Mutant Mice.
evidence.snippet: we present the first demonstration of a potential definitive treatment  that significantly improves optic and sciatic nerve atrophy, sensory neuropathy,  and mitochondrial dysfunction in FDXR-related mitochondriopathy

nodes.description: Bilateral auditory neuropathy in all eight founding patients.

evidence.reference_title: FDXR Mutations Cause Sensorial Neuropathies and Expand the Spectrum of Mitochondrial Fe-S-Synthesis Diseases.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report on eight subjects from four independent families affected by auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy.

nodes.description: Attenuated retinal vessels appearing as white lines on the fundus in three of five patients in one ocular cohort, with completely occluded vessels, delayed filling and peripheral non-perfusion on fluorescein angiography. Those authors propose retinal vascular occlusion as a distinct feature of FDXR disease; it has not been reported in the other cohorts.

evidence.reference_title: FDXR-associated disease in a Chinese cohort: Unraveling expanded ocular phenotypes and genetic spectrum.
evidence.snippet: fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) further revealed vascular  abnormalities including delayed filling, completely occluded retinal  vasculature, and severe retinal vascular nonperfusion of the peripheral retina.

nodes.description: Hearing aids, remote-microphone systems and low-vision rehabilitation for the combined sensory impairment. In auditory neuropathy, speech discrimination is worse than the pure-tone audiogram predicts, so amplification alone performs less well than it does in cochlear hearing loss. Cochlear implantation has been reported in a single adult case.

Biallelic germline FDXR variants, over eighty per cent of them missense and several clustering in the FAD-binding site. No patient with two truncating alleles has been reported, from which the authors infer that complete loss of FDXR function is not compatible with life, so the disease alleles are hypomorphic rather than null.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic mutations in the ferredoxin reductase gene cause novel mitochondriopathy with optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: these data provide the first demonstration that germline,  hypomorphic mutations in FDXR cause a novel mitochondriopathy and optic atrophy  in humans

nodes.description: Patient fibroblasts show low oxygen consumption, reduced respiratory complex activities and reduced ATP production, with raised reactive oxygen species. The membrane potential falls with it.

evidence.snippet: the carrier frequency of the p.Arg386Trp variant was  estimated as 1 of 185 in the Mexican population

nodes.description: A homozygous missense knock-in, originally found as a recessive gait mutant, carrying the mouse equivalent of a human FDXR substitution. It is the model behind the optic and transport findings in this entry's pathograph: visual acuity is reduced on optokinetic testing, retinal ganglion cell layer nuclei are lost by six months, and optic axonal transport is defective.

Cluster assembly fails for want of reducing equivalents, and the cluster-dependent enzymes follow: mitochondrial and cytosolic aconitase and the complex II subunit SDHB are all reduced in patient fibroblasts. This is the rate-limiting step of the disease.

evidence.reference_title: FDXR Mutations Cause Sensorial Neuropathies and Expand the Spectrum of Mitochondrial Fe-S-Synthesis Diseases.
evidence.snippet: ISC proteins are involved in enzymatic catalysis, gene expression, and DNA replication and repair.

evidence.reference_title: Integrated analysis of the molecular pathogenesis of FDXR-associated disease.
evidence.snippet: Our previous studies have demonstrated that hypomorphic mutations in FDXR cause a novel mitochondriopathy and optic atrophy in humans and mice, attributed in part to reduced function of the electron transport chain (ETC) as well as elevated production of reactive oxygen species (ROS).

nodes.description: With cluster supply short, the cell reads itself as iron-starved, so iron import continues past need. Iron handling is deregulated in patient fibroblasts, with evidence of mitochondrial iron overload that the authors themselves call indirect.

evidence.reference_title: FDXR Mutations Cause Sensorial Neuropathies and Expand the Spectrum of Mitochondrial Fe-S-Synthesis Diseases.
evidence.snippet: We observed deregulated iron homeostasis in FDXR mutant fibroblasts and indirect evidence of mitochondrial iron overload.

nodes.description: Iron accumulates in mitochondria, shown directly in mouse tissue where the founding human evidence was indirect. Excess mitochondrial iron favours free-radical formation, which is the link from the iron branch to the oxidative one.

evidence.snippet: Molecular analysis indicates that FDXR mutation also leads to mitochondrial iron overload and an associated depolarization of the mitochondrial membrane

nodes.description: Bilateral optic atrophy in all eight founding patients. It is not universal across the spectrum: one patient in a later cohort had no visual problem over sixteen years of follow-up.

evidence.reference_title: FDXR Mutations Cause Sensorial Neuropathies and Expand the Spectrum of Mitochondrial Fe-S-Synthesis Diseases.
evidence.snippet: eight subjects from four independent families affected by auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic mutations in the ferredoxin reductase gene cause novel mitochondriopathy with optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: we conducted whole-exome sequencing  of patients with optic atrophy and other neurological signs of mitochondriopathy  and identified 17 individuals from 13 unrelated families with recessive  mutations in FDXR

nodes.description: The two branches converge here: reduced respiratory chain function raises reactive oxygen species, and mitochondrial iron overload depolarizes the membrane and favours free-radical formation. The authors place this convergence behind the neurodegeneration.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic mutations in the ferredoxin reductase gene cause novel mitochondriopathy with optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: Excessive levels of iron favor the formation of excess oxygen free radicals and consequent mitochondrial dysfunction.

nodes.description: Sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy in about 23 per cent of reported FDXR patients across the whole spectrum. It may begin acutely enough to be mistaken for an acquired inflammatory neuropathy, which is the differential that review was written about.

evidence.reference_title: FDXR-associated disease: a challenging differential diagnosis with inflammatory peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: significant incidence of sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy (22.72%) and  ataxia (43.18%)

evidence.reference_title: FDXR-associated disease: a challenging differential diagnosis with inflammatory peripheral neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: a peripheral  neuropathy which can mimic an acute inflammatory disease

nodes.description: FDXR passes electrons from NADPH to the mitochondrial ferredoxins, which deliver the reducing equivalents that cluster assembly consumes, both for building the nascent cluster on the scaffold and for the reductive fusion step. The lesion is therefore in the electron supply to the pathway rather than in any scaffold, carrier or transporter, which distinguishes this disease from its siblings.

evidence.reference_title: Integrated analysis of the molecular pathogenesis of FDXR-associated disease.
evidence.snippet: The mitochondrial flavoprotein ferredoxin reductase (FDXR) is required for biogenesis of iron-sulfur clusters and for steroidogenesis.

nodes.description: FDXR is the only human ferredoxin reductase. Its activity in patient fibroblasts is roughly half of control, which is enough to impair the pathway it feeds without being lethal.

evidence.reference_title: FDXR Mutations Cause Sensorial Neuropathies and Expand the Spectrum of Mitochondrial Fe-S-Synthesis Diseases.
evidence.snippet: FDXR encodes the mitochondrial ferredoxin reductase, the sole human ferredoxin reductase implicated in the biosynthesis of iron-sulfur clusters (ISCs) and in heme formation.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic mutations in the ferredoxin reductase gene cause novel mitochondriopathy with optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: Ferredoxin NADP reductase activity in patient fibroblasts, non-transduced patient fibroblasts, and patient fibroblasts overexpressing FDXR (rescued) were 48%, 53%, and 94% respectively of the mean value measured for age and gender matched control fibroblasts.

nodes.description: Beyond the ganglion-cell loss of optic atrophy, several cohorts show a retinal dystrophy with severely impaired cone and rod responses in the first decades, and in three of five patients in one ocular cohort attenuated retinal vessels appearing as white lines, with occlusion and delayed filling on angiography. Those authors propose retinal vascular occlusion as a distinct feature of FDXR disease. Its mechanism is unknown and it is not connected to an upstream node here.

evidence.snippet: all patients presented with retinal dystrophy, and electroretinogram showed  severely impaired cone and rod functions in their first decades

nodes.description: The long sensory projections fail. Mouse work shows significant optic transport defects, which the authors read as the basis of the optic atrophy, together with neurodegenerative cell loss in the central nervous system. The corresponding cochlear lesion is post-synaptic rather than cochlear: brainstem responses are lost while otoacoustic emissions, which report outer hair cell function, are preserved.
